rows.subtype: Approach: seeking help from teacher or tutor [Action]
rows.description: The student stays back after class, shows the last three test papers to the teacher, and agrees on a twice-weekly doubt session, which is cheaper and more targeted than a full extra coaching batch.

rows.subtype: Approach: avoidance by studying favourite subjects [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student keeps revising English and Biology because they feel good, while Maths gets skipped. Marks in strong subjects rise slightly, but the failing subject continues to drag the overall result.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, analogy, batching, commitment device, cutting losses, experiment and measure

rows.subtype: Approach: minimum viable version with small wins [Action]
rows.description: Rather than aiming to jump from 30 to 80, the student targets 45 in the next test by mastering only the easiest question types first, which builds confidence and a working routine.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, analogy, avoidance and procrastination, batching, commitment device, cutting losses

rows.subtype: Approach: blaming the teacher or the syllabus [Pitfall]
rows.description: The student decides the teacher is bad and the paper unfair. This protects self-esteem for a while but produces no plan, so the next test result is the same and the deadline is closer.

rows.subtype: Approach: analogy with a learning strategy that worked [Thinking]
rows.description: The student recalls that drawing diagrams fixed a weak Geography unit, and tries the same approach for Physics by sketching circuits and force diagrams before attempting numericals.

rows.subtype: Approach: experiment and measure over two weeks [Action]
rows.description: The student tries two methods, reading solved examples versus attempting problems first, tracks quiz scores for each for two weeks, and keeps the method that gave clearly better results.

rows.subtype: Approach: peer study group with accountability [Action]
rows.description: Three classmates meet twice a week to explain problems to each other. Explaining exposes gaps, and the promise to show up keeps the weakest student attending even when motivation dips.

rows.subtype: Approach: noticing no improvement and switching method [Revision]
rows.description: After a month of re-reading notes with little score change, the student admits passive reading is not working and shifts to closed-book practice questions, which quickly shows real weak spots.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, analogy, avoidance and procrastination, batching, commitment device, cutting losses

rows.subtype: Approach: cutting losses on one weak unit [Revision]
rows.description: Realising one chapter costs hours for few marks, the student agrees with the teacher to secure the pass through other units first and return to the hard chapter only if time remains.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: accountability partner, analogy, avoidance and procrastination, batching, commitment device, experiment and measure

rows.subtype: Approach: maximising with a decision matrix [Thinking]
rows.description: After Class 10, a student scores Science, Commerce and Humanities on interest, marks trend, career options, cost and family support. Weighting each makes trade-offs visible rather than felt vaguely.
